konzil: verdunklung der kirche , p. 264) and st. bellarmine writes: original: “ich antworte, dass [...] ein solcher [namlich der ungerecht exkommunizierte] sich aufgrund ausserer gemeinschaft innerhalb der kirche befindet, die den menschen im eigentlichen sinne zum glied jener sichtbaren kirche macht.” translation: “i answer that [...] such a person [namely the unjustly excommunicated] is within the church by reason of external communion, which makes a man a member of that visible church in the proper sense.” (quoted in 2. vatikanisches konzil: verdunklung der kirche , p. 267) 7. overall conclusion original: “wenn aber wir oder gar ein engel vom himmel euch ein anderes evangelium verkunden als das, das wir euch verkundet haben - er sei verflucht!” (gal 1,8) translation: “but even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a different gospel from the one we preached to you - let him be accursed!” (gal 1:8) saint paul establishes a principle[100] that carries the whole defense presented here. the binding force of ecclesiastical authority is not limitless, but bound to the truth it serves. so much so that even an apostle or an angel from heaven would fall under anathema if he preached another gospel. this precise relationship between truth and authority is the standard by which the resistance of the fsspx must be measured, and by which, as i have tried to show, it is justified. the starting point was the diagnosis of the crisis. modernism, condemned by pius x as the “synthesis of all heresies,” reduces, in the interpretation defended here, the world to the realm of becoming and denies the realm of being, from which follows relativism in doctrine, liturgy, and morals. this crisis is not hypothetical. it can be seen in measurable indicators: in the loss of faith regarding transubstantiation, in the voting behavior of whole episcopal conferences, in the state of belief among the clergy according to studies, and in the absence of any canonical reaction to publicly modernist teaching. because modernism thus systematically endangers the salvation of souls, and because salus animarum suprema lex applies, the same basic question arises for the three points of fsspx resistance - the refusal regarding v2, regarding the novus ordo , and the episcopal consecrations without mandate: whether fidelity to the received truth not only permits but demands disobedience toward current discipline. on the first point, it was shown that the criticized passages of v2 were not proclaimed infallibly but belong to authentic, non-infallible magisterium, toward which dissent is possible under qualified conditions. this follows from the basic principle that a doctrine which is in principle capable of error and whose truth content is naturally knowable cannot oblige contradictionless assent, and it is expressly confirmed by pre-conciliar manual theology in ott and van noort. that dignitatis humanae , lumen gentium viii, and lumen gentium xvi contradict received doctrine in their natural reading was demonstrated in detail; and by the example of saint maximus, who presumed good intention in honorius but nevertheless would never have signed a formula readable as heretical, it was shown that good intention does not annul the objective statement of a text. the section on the heresies justified by v2 - from the alleged continuance of the old covenant, through the condemned ecumenism of return, to participation in non-catholic services - further showed how grave the crisis is and how little the faithful today can rely on receiving unadulterated doctrine from their shepherds. on the second point, father gaudron’s formal argument was refined in the moderate position. the novus ordo is bad in itself as a rite, not because every mass celebrated according to it would be bad, but because, as a rite, it leaves too much room to obscure the sacrificial character and thereby fails privatively to fulfill an essential task of the mass. since the law prescribing such a rite does not serve the common good of the church, it does not bind in conscience according to the principle lex injusta non obligat . for the fsspx there is the additional point that celebrating the novus ordo would mean revoking a substantively never-refuted criticism and would thereby spiritually harm those faithful who rely on its seriousness: a scandalum pusillorum in the sense of saint thomas. on the third and most serious point, the episcopal consecrations, several independent arguments converge. the prohibition is not divine law, for episcopal consecration does not necessarily confer jurisdiction, as the classic cases of auxiliary, titular, and retired bishops show, so that the prohibition is divine law only insofar as someone arrogates universal jurisdiction to himself, which the fsspx precisely does not do. since it is therefore merely positive church law, two meta-juridical principles apply. epikie provides a good, though not coercive, argument, because the original legislator enacted the prohibition against the usurpation of the episcopal office by secular powers, not against the internal church emergency in which the fsspx intends precisely to preserve the received order. the decisive argument is necessitas , the priority of the highest law, the salvation of souls, over positive law. eda’s determination that no state of necessity existed is not an infallible doctrinal judgment but a fallible factual determination outside the limits of infallibility drawn by pastor aeternus , as shown by the cases of athanasius and eusebius of dorylaeum, whose independent resistance was later explicitly confirmed by the church. the objection of private jurisdiction fails because the fsspx proves by its very self-limitation that it claims no comprehensive power of disposal over the laws. the consecrations are also not schismatic, because schism according to naz, thomas, and cajetan presupposes a fundamental, habitual rejection of papal authority, which the fsspx does not enact; and finally, they incur no valid automatic penalty because according to canons 1323 and 1324, even unculpable error, indeed even culpable error, about the existence of a state of necessity excludes latae sententiae excommunication. the decisive question remains whether the path of the fsspx really was the right one, or whether a less drastic path would have sufficed. the answer is that no such path exists. the ecclesia dei communities preserve the traditional liturgy, but they are bound to full acceptance of v2 and cannot publicly name the problematic texts as contradicting tradition. whoever wants to fight the crisis at its root must be able to do precisely that. silent resistance within the existing structures fails even more fundamentally because it cannot be extended to priestly formation, and tradition therefore breaks off over two generations. without independent seminaries and without bishops who supervise these seminaries and ordain new priests, the resistance has no future. the episcopal consecrations of 1988 were therefore not an excess, but the proportionally minimal means that made the resistance reproducible beyond the death of its founder. this is precisely the meaning of the pauline principle with which this conclusion began. where an authority, however high, effectively favors another gospel, disobedience is not infidelity; obedience is. the fsspx has not left the church; in a state of necessity, with the least means sufficient for the task, it preserved what the church has always taught and celebrated. in this, and not in rebellion against the petrine office, lies the justification of its path and of its episcopal consecrations. 8. further relevant points here i want to touch on a few further relevant points that are not necessary for the arguments presented, but should answer some questions that may arise. 8.1. van noort on disciplinary infallibility a critic might appeal, against several of the previous arguments, especially against the necessitas argument and against the no section, to the manualist teaching on the church’s secondary infallibility regarding general discipline. this teaching deserves its own treatment, because its most prominent representative, msgr. gerard van noort (1861-1946), carries great weight as one of the leading pre-conciliar dogmatic theologians. van noort’s three-volume tractatus apologetici et dogmatici was for decades a standard textbook in the seminaries of the universal church; pius xi appointed him domestic prelate in 1934 and gave him a roman honorary doctorate; and msgr. joseph clifford fenton, the most prominent defender of traditional theology under pius xii, counted him among the indispensable manualists of the twentieth century. whoever simply brushes van noort aside therefore fails not only to meet the burden of proof, but makes precisely the mistake the modernists always accused manual theology of making. in christ’s church (dogmatic theology vol. ii, ed. castelot/murphy, newman press 1957, assertion 3, pp. 113-115), van noort maintains as theologically certain the thesis that the church’s infallibility also extends to general discipline: “the church’s infallibility extends to the general discipline of the church. this proposition is theologically certain. by the term ‘general discipline of the church’ are meant those ecclesiastical laws passed for the universal church for the direction of christian worship and christian living.” on careful reading, however, this thesis supports our argument rather than contradicting it, because van noort precisely restricts its scope in three successive steps. first, within every disciplinary law he distinguishes two judgments, one doctrinal and one practical: “when the church’s rulers sanction a law, they implicitly make a twofold judgment: 1. ‘this law squares with the church’s doctrine of faith and morals’; that is, it imposes nothing that is at odds with sound belief and good morals. this amounts to a doctrinal decree. 2. ‘this law, considering all the circumstances, is most opportune.’ this is a decree of practical judgment.” (ibid., p. 114) only the first judgment concerns secondary infallibility. the second, the practical judgment, van noort expressly excludes from infallibility: “although it would be rash to cast aspersions on the timeliness of a law, especially at the very moment when the church imposes or expressly reaffirms it, still the church does not claim to be infallible in issuing a decree of practical judgment . for the church’s rulers were never promised the highest degree of prudence for the conduct of affairs.” (ibid., p. 114, emphasis here) second, even the positive scope of his thesis is narrowly defined. what it excludes are universal laws that are “at odds with faith or morality” or “by its very nature conducive to the injury of souls” (ibid., p. 114). as historical evidence, van noort cites the condemnation of the jansenist synod of pistoia by pius vi in auctorem fidei (1794), where the following is rejected: “that the church could establish discipline which would be dangerous, harmful, and conducive to superstition and materialism” (dh 2602). the class of examples by which van noort’s thesis is oriented is therefore active falsification , such as discipline that leads to superstition or materialism, not every form of inexpediency or privative deficiency. third, and this is already classically embedded in thomistic law, the class of non-binding unjust laws according to st i-ii q.96 a.4 is significantly broader than the class of laws that van noort protects from false ecclesial sanction. thomas lists, as conditions for lex injusta , among other things failure to promote the common good, exceeding the lawgiver’s authority, and unequal distribution. van noort’s protection, by contrast, applies only when a law actively harms by its nature. a law can fail sufficiently to promote the common good of the church and therefore not bind the conscience as lex injusta without falling into the narrow class prohibited by van noort. when we apply this to our previous argument, two clear findings emerge. on the one hand, the necessitas argument fits seamlessly into van noort’s schema. the statement in eda that no state of necessity exists is not the doctrinal assertion “episcopal consecrations without mandate are incompatible with faith and morals,” but the practical judgment “in the circumstances of 1988 there is no state of necessity that would justify such consecrations.” van noort himself removes such judgments from infallibility. thus, from traditional manual theology, he confirms exactly what we derived above from pastor aeternus and ott. on the other hand, the no arguments also do not come into conflict with van noort, provided they are read correctly in thomistic terms. the thesis of this document is not that the no is actively heretical or superstitious, but that it privatively fails to fulfill its task of clearly expressing the essence of the mass, and that the law prescribing it does not sufficiently serve the common good of the church. both claims lie categorically outside van noort’s protected scope. privative deficiency in the sense of the thomistic determination of evil as privatio of the due good is conceptually different from by its very nature conducive to the injury of souls , which is what van noort means and what he exemplifies by the condemnation of pistoia. the only point at which the no threatened to become actively heretical in the strict sense was the original definition in igmr 7. precisely there, however, it was corrected shortly after promulgation, which incidentally speaks rather against the assumption that the magisterium universally sanctioned a law harmful by its very nature . whoever wants to refute the no argument by appeal to van noort would therefore have to show that the no as a rite is by its very nature conducive to the injury of souls . but that is precisely not claimed in this document. what is claimed is that the no is privatively deficient and does not sufficiently serve the common good of the church. both are logically compatible with van noort, because the doctrine of lex injusta in thomas recognizes a broader class of non-binding laws than that narrow class in which van noort sees the church protected from false universal sanction. as van noort himself emphasizes in the corollary to assertion 3, disciplinary infallibility harmonizes: “beautifully with the mutability of even universal laws. for a law, even though it be thoroughly consonant with revealed truth, can, given a change in circumstances, become less timely or even useless, so that prudence may dictate its abrogation or modification.” (ibid., p. 114) for van noort, the mutability even of universal laws according to prudence is not a contradiction of his infallibility thesis, but its natural complement. thus the position of manual theology, represented by its authoritative witness, is not only compatible with the arguments of this document, but supports them at decisive points. 8.2. have the gates of hell prevailed over the church? an objection brought against every form of crisis diagnosis is this: if the crisis is really as grave as i have claimed above, and if the fsspx really must resort to episcopal consecrations against current law, then christ’s promise seems to lose its force. original: “du bist petrus, der fels, und auf diesen felsen werde ich meine kirche bauen, und die machte der unterwelt werden sie nicht uberwaltigen” (mt 16,18). translation: “you are peter, the rock, and upon this rock i will build my church, and the powers of the underworld will not prevail against it” (mt 16:18). whoever assumes a crisis of this magnitude, so the objection goes, would have to admit that hell has prevailed. what the promise guarantees must be stated precisely. it does not guarantee that the church will suffer no grave crises, but that she will not perish and that her faith will not be extinguished. a victory of hell would be the extinction of the church or the complete extinguishing of the received faith. neither is manifestly the case today. the received faith is handed on in the fsspx, in other traditional communities, in faithful bishops, priests, and laity; the holy see is occupied; the sacrament of the altar is celebrated in countless churches. the question is therefore not whether the gates of hell have prevailed, but whether a crisis of this type and this magnitude is compatible with the promise. a look at church history answers precisely this question negatively, that is, such crises have in fact already been passed through repeatedly without the promise being considered broken. on the doctrinal axis, the arian crisis of the fourth century is the most impressive case. at the parallel synods of rimini and seleucia (359), under political pressure from emperor constantius ii, most western and eastern bishops signed an arian or semi-arian-readable formula in which the homoousios was abandoned. jerome summarizes the situation in a sentence that has since become proverbial (jerome, dialogus contra luciferianos 19, pl 23, 181, latin full text: [101]; english translation: [102]): original: “tunc usiae nomen abolitum est: tunc nicaenae fidei damnatio conclamata est. ingemuit totus orbis, et arianum se esse miratus est.” translation: “then the word usia was abolished; then the condemnation of the nicene faith was proclaimed. the whole world groaned and was amazed to find itself arian.” athanasius at times stood practically alone against a large part of the episcopate, athanasius contra mundum , and this with the explicit approval of tradition, which later honored him as a doctor of the church. liberius i have already treated above; he belongs to the same line. the crisis stretched from nicaea (325) to constantinople i (381), that is, over more than half a century. no one concluded from it that the gates of hell had prevailed. on the axis of papal error, beyond the cases already treated of honorius and nicholas i, the case of john xxii is especially significant. between 1331 and 1334, in several sermons at avignon, he taught that the souls of the just do not behold god immediately after death, but only after the general resurrection. theologians publicly contradicted him; on the eve of his death, john xxii retracted his position in the bull ne super his . his successor benedict xii defined the opposite de fide in 1336 in the dogmatic constitution benedictus deus (benedict xii, benedictus deus , january 29, 1336, dh 1000-1002, latin full text on vatican.va: [103]; english translation: [104]): original: “ animae sanctorum omnium... mox post mortem ipsorum... fuerunt, sunt et erunt in caelo,... viderunt et vident divinam essentiam visione intuitiva et etiam faciali ” translation: “the souls of all the saints... immediately after their death... have been, are, and will be in heaven,... they have seen and see the divine essence by intuitive and even face-to-face vision” a reigning pope publicly preached against the later de fide definition, retracted it himself, and his successor dogmatized the opposite. here too no one concluded from the event that christ’s promise had been invalidated. on the moral axis, the situation in church history has several times sunk so low that today’s scandals recede behind it. in the saeculum obscurum (ca. 904-964), the papacy at times became the plaything of roman families. sergius iii ascended the throne in 904 after his predecessor leo v and the antipope christopher had allegedly been murdered at his instigation. stephen vi’s synodus horrenda , the cadaver synod of 897, had the exhumed corpse of pope formosus brought to trial in pontifical vestments, posthumously condemned, had three fingers of his right hand cut off, and thrown into the tiber. john xii was deposed in 963 by a synod in rome convened by otto i for murder, perjury, incest, simony, idolatry, and a long list of further crimes; the detailed account is given by the eyewitness liutprand of cremona in his historia ottonis , chapters 4-12 (english translation with source reference: [105]). benedict ix sold the papacy in 1045 to his godfather, who then reigned as gregory vi, and later returned once more as a claimant. the renaissance papacy under alexander vi borgia (1492-1503) continued with open illegitimate children, dynastic nepotism, and political murder campaigns. in none of these cases did anyone conclude from the scandal that the gates of hell had prevailed or that the sacraments were henceforth invalid. on the axis of visible unity, the western schism (1378-1417) is the sharpest comparison. after the death of gregory xi, urban vi was first elected in rome in 1378; then the same cardinals, claiming their own election invalid because of pressure from the roman populace, elected clement vii in avignon. both claimed the papacy. in 1409 the council of pisa attempted to end the division by declaring both deposed and electing alexander v; since those deposed did not abandon their claims, after that there were three simultaneous claimants to the papacy. geographically, christendom was roughly divided as follows: before pisa, france, scotland, castile, aragon, sicily, naples, and the papal states adhered to the avignon line; the empire, england, italy outside the south, scandinavia, poland, and hungary to the roman line. after pisa, france, england, portugal, bohemia, prussia, and parts of italy and the empire switched to the pisan line; spain and scotland remained with avignon; naples, poland, bavaria, and parts of the empire remained with rome (cf. wikipedia , western schism , [106], and council of pisa , [107]). the annuario pontificio today recognizes the roman line, that is, urban vi, boniface ix, innocent vii, and gregory xii, as legitimate. on the basis of established population estimates for the late middle ages (western christendom overall about 45-50 million, france alone 12-15 million, the empire 10-12 million, the iberian peninsula 5-6 million), the adherents can be roughly quantified: before pisa, an estimated 40 to 45% of latin christendom adhered to the avignon line, today regarded as illegitimate, and about 50 to 55% to the roman. after pisa, the ratios turned drastically: the pisan line, also regarded today as illegitimate, was recognized by about 55 to 60% of christendom, the avignon line by about 10 to 15%, so that only about 15 to 20% remained with the line today recognized as the only legitimate roman line. this means concretely: at the height of the confusion, roughly four out of five catholics adhered to popes who are today classified as antipopes. saints stood on different sides: catherine of siena supported the roman line, vincent ferrer at first the avignon line and changed only late. at that time it was epistemically certain for no one to know who the true pope was. here too no one concluded from this enormous confusion that the gates of hell had prevailed. on the contrary, the crisis was overcome in 1417 at the council of constance with the election of martin v. thus every aspect of the present crisis that the objector would have to classify as unprecedented is covered by a historical precedent. doctrinal pressure across the hierarchy: the arian crisis. papal error in a doctrinally relevant question: honorius, nicholas i, john xxii. moral corruption at the top: saeculum obscurum , renaissance papacy. long duration: the arian crisis more than half a century, the schism 39 years, the pornocratic age around 60 years. massive confusion over the lawful line and factual loyalty of majorities to antipopes: the schism. if none of these cases counted as a victory of the gates of hell, then the present state does not either. in addition, a pattern stands out from church history: every severe crisis was historically followed by a phase of purification and dogmatic clarification in which the church emerged strengthened from the upheaval. constantinople i (381) followed arianism with the definitive establishment of trinitarian dogmatics; benedictus deus (1336) followed john xxii with the dogmatic clarification of the immediate vision of god; the cluniac and later gregorian reform followed the saeculum obscurum ; the council of constance (1417) followed the schism with reunification; the council of trent (1545-1563) followed the reformation with the counter-reformation renewal; vatican i (1869-1870) followed gallicanism, enlightenment, and revolution with the dogmatic definition of the petrine office. this is the pattern in which christ’s promise historically realizes itself: not by avoiding crises, but by preserving the faith through them, often through small remnants, followed by a renewal of the whole church. mt 16:18 is therefore not invalidated. on the contrary, that in the midst of the present crisis traditional bishops are consecrated, that the received rite is celebrated in countless places, that religious communities, seminaries, and families hand on the catholic faith in full, is itself evidence that the gates of hell have not prevailed over the church. whoever wants to infer from the gravity of the crisis a victory of hell would have to do the same, with equal consistency, for the arian crisis, the saeculum obscurum , and the western schism, which no one has ever done. the promise holds, but it holds in the mode of testing in crisis and purification, not as a guarantee of a frictionless course. 8.3. but the fsspx has no jurisdiction the fsspx indeed has no ordinary jurisdiction and has never claimed to have it. this lack of jurisdiction endangers only the liceity of the sacraments of marriage and confession. in these cases the principle ecclesia supplet applies, according to which in an emergency the church supplies the necessary jurisdiction. that a state of emergency exists we have already seen above. 8.4. sedevacantism the critical statements i made above about v2 could give the impression that my position ultimately leads to sedevacantism. if the popes of the post-conciliar period teach or tolerate heresies, and if a heretical pope according to traditional doctrine is no longer pope, then it seems logically to follow that the sees of rome have been vacant since v2. i do not draw this conclusion, and the reason lies in a distinction firmly rooted in church history. the thesis that a heretical pope loses his office goes back, in the form most often cited today, to bellarmine. in de romano pontifice lib. ii, cap. 30 he writes (full text: [108], cf. [109]): original: “quinta opinio vera est: papa haereticus manifestus per se desinit esse papa et caput, sicut per se desinit esse christianus et membrum corporis ecclesiae: quare ab ecclesia iudicari et puniri potest.” translation: “the fifth opinion is true: a manifestly heretical pope ceases of himself to be pope and head, just as he ceases of himself to be a christian and member of the body of the church; wherefore he can be judged and punished by the church.” bellarmine precisely limits this thesis in the same chapter. he speaks exclusively of the haereticus manifestus , the publicly professing heretic, and expressly excludes the hidden heretic, who remains a member of the church and therefore pope. mere suspicion, error, or a misunderstood word therefore precisely do not suffice. what is decisive for applying this doctrine to a concrete case is the canonical-theological distinction between material and formal heresy. one is materially heretical if one maintains a statement that is objectively incompatible with catholic teaching without being conscious of the contradiction or without, after sufficient correction, persisting in one’s error with pertinacious obstinacy. one is formally heretical only if one denies a revealed truth with full knowledge and precisely such pertinacity. bellarmine’s thesis presupposes formal heresy, because otherwise the condition of consciously leaving the church is not fulfilled. whoever merely errs materially has not separated himself from the church, but remains in a state of teachability. this distinction is not academic, but has a prominent church-historical application that is structurally parallel to the present situation. pope honorius i (625-638), in his letter to patriarch sergius, used the formula that in christ there is one will ( unam voluntatem ), and the third council of constantinople condemned him posthumously in 681 in session xiii as a supporter of monothelitism. it was maximus the confessor, one of the most important saints and confessor-martyrs of the eastern church, who defended honorius against the accusation of formal heresy. in his letter to the priest marinus of cyprus (ca. 641), maximus argues that by the formula one will honorius had merely meant that christ had no conflicting fleshly will of concupiscence, since he was conceived and born without sin. maximus relies for this on the witness of john symponus, the secretary who had drafted the letter for honorius (cf. catholic encyclopedia , “st. maximus of constantinople,” [110]). in a later letter to the patrician peter, maximus even calls honorius “the great honorius” and places him in line with his unquestionably orthodox successors severinus and john iv. what maximus does here, precisely, is to mark the difference between a materially ambiguous formulation and formal heresy. honorius used words readable in a heretical sense, but he did not mean them with heretical intent. i follow exactly this distinction with regard to the post-conciliar popes. they approved or taught texts that, in one reading, contradict received doctrine, but they did not set themselves in pertinacious obstinacy against better-known catholic truth; rather, they operate within a theological framework in which they subjectively believe themselves to be compatible with tradition. a second precedent supports this. pope nicholas i (858-867) declared in his responsa ad consulta bulgarorum of november 866, cap. 104 (full text: [111]; also mansi xv, 401-434): original: “si vero in nomine sanctae trinitatis vel tantum in nomine christi, sicut in actibus apostolorum legimus (...) baptizati sunt, (...) constat eos non esse denuo baptizandos.” translation: “but if they were baptized in the name of the holy trinity or only in the name of christ, as we read in the acts of the apostles (...), it is clear that they are not to be baptized again.” a baptism only in the name of christ is therefore equivalent to the trinitarian form and is not to be repeated. this statement contradicts the later teaching that the trinitarian form is prescribed necessitate sacramenti , as the council of florence held in 1439 in the decretum pro armenis : original: “forma autem est: ego te baptizo in nomine patris et filii et spiritus sancti.” (dh 1314) translation: “the form, however, is: i baptize you in the name of the father and of the son and of the holy spirit.” (dh 1314) nicholas i therefore erred in a doctrinally relevant question. but no one in church history has ever claimed that he therefore lost the petrine office or was not a true pope. he is still venerated today as saint nicholas the great; all subsequent popes considered his official acts valid; his cardinal appointments remained uncontested. this shows that a material error in the non-infallible papal magisterium does not abolish the papacy as such. otherwise one would have to deny the pontificate not only of nicholas i, but also the validity of all appointments and ordinations he performed, with consequences for apostolic succession that no one has ever drawn. thus the concern for the visibility of the church is not endangered either. pastor aeternus chapter 2 (ds 3056-3058) teaches de fide that the petrine office endures perpetually in the roman pontiffs, and christ himself promised to be with his church “all days, even to the end of the world” (mt 28:20). pius xii emphasizes in mystici corporis christi (1943, aas 35, 199-248) the indestructible visibility of the one church of christ. if the popes since v2 err only materially and not formally, then they remain true popes, the petrine office remains occupied, and the visibility of the church is preserved. there is no hidden sedevacantist state that would collide with this doctrine. but this does not reinstate the duty to accept every non-infallible papal teaching. materially heretical statements, or statements objectively incompatible with received doctrine, remain substantively false, regardless of whether their author himself holds them pertinaciously or not. i may therefore at the same time recognize that the post-conciliar popes are true popes and refuse to assent to those statements that depart from the objective finding of tradition. this precise double attitude is the position of the fsspx. it is not sedevacantism, because it does not deny the papacy; nor is it modernist accommodation, because it places truth above the claimed authority. it therefore follows precisely the model maximus the confessor showed in the case of honorius, and it is fully compatible with the dogmatic teaching on the visibility and perpetuity of the church.[112] 8.5. proportionality after all the arguments in this document, only the prudential objection remains that episcopal consecration, as the most drastic and canonically sanctioned step, exceeded what was proportionally necessary, because the survival of tradition did not depend on the bishops of precisely this community. this objection misunderstands what proportionality means in a state of necessity. what is required is not the mildest conceivable means as such, but the mildest means still sufficient to remedy the necessity. a means that does not remedy the necessity is not a milder alternative, but simply not an alternative. that is exactly the case with the non-episcopal paths. the diagnosed necessity is not a punctual event like the starving man’s theft in thomas, but a structural crisis extending over generations. but priests can be ordained only by a bishop, and priests die. without a bishop who shares the diagnosis and ordains men trained in the critique, the entire resistance ends with the death of the last bishop favorable to it. a resistance without its own bishops is therefore not a more measured resistance, but a resistance with a built-in expiration date. the consecrations were therefore not greater drasticness, but the minimum capable of withstanding the duration and nature of the necessity at all. this also shifts the burden of proof: the critic would not have to show that a milder path was conceivable, but that it would have sufficed. the appeal to the claim that god will preserve tradition by other means in any case does not help the objection. this argument proves too much, for by the same logic no human effort to preserve the faith would ever be necessary: athanasius too would not have had to resist, since god could have preserved the nicene faith even without him. providence, however, ordinarily works not past responsible secondary causes, but through them. the promise of mt 16:18 guarantees the result, that the church will not perish, but not the dispensability of any particular means, and it is not a free pass for inaction. in history it has always realized itself precisely through those remnants that acted in the crisis. the question of the one acting is therefore never the abstract one whether the church will survive, but the concrete one whether this is the means available to him to avert a foreseeable grave loss. added to this is the asymmetry of risks that guides every prudent decision under uncertainty. the loss of the episcopal line would have been irreversible in the relevant period: if the favorable bishops die without successors, one can no longer ordain, and the formation tradition breaks off. the costs of the consecrations, by contrast - the canonical penalties and the irregular status - were reversible, and in fact they were partially withdrawn when benedict xvi lifted the excommunications in 2009 and francis granted faculties for confession in 2015. whoever must choose between a reversible harm and an irreversible loss chooses prudently when he prevents the irreversible loss. the later partial normalization confirmed precisely this: the harm incurred was healable; the loss avoided would not have been. finally, that the mildest sufficient means was chosen, and not maximalism, is shown by the self-limitation of the consecrations themselves. only the power of orders, indispensable for the reproduction of the priesthood, was taken, and precisely not the jurisdiction that would have made the bishops into a parallel hierarchy. even within the drastic step, therefore, the minimal form was chosen. proportionality is finally to be judged ex ante , according to the foresight reasonably possible for the one acting: a dying founder, a consent repeatedly delayed in his justified perception, and therefore the realistic expectation that the window would close with his death. a means granted only afterward would have been equivalent ex ante to no means being granted at all. more than prudential certainty cannot be reached here, because prudential judgments by their nature are not proofs. but the combination of these considerations - that every milder path would not have remedied the necessity, and that this insufficiency in fact later proved itself - compresses the remaining the internet medieval sourcebook. https://sourcebooks.web.fordham.edu/basis/866nicholas-bulgar.asp [112] even if one did not share the classification defended here of the post-conciliar popes as erring only materially, not formally, and instead assumed formal heresy, the argument would not necessarily lead to sedevacantism. in what follows i sketch my own admittedly novel solution to the problem, which i do not present as the standard position of the fsspx, but as a reserve argument for the hypothetical case that someone did not want to apply the distinction between material and formal heresy to these popes. structurally similar, though mechanically formulated differently, is the cassiciacum thesis of mgr. guerard des lauriers (1979, cahiers de cassiciacum ), which distinguishes between a materialiter and a formaliter pope and has the same problem in view. three propositions are in tension here. first, bellarmine’s teaching that a manifest formally heretical pope loses his office ipso facto ( de romano pontifice lib. ii, cap. 30, https://www.fisheaters.com/bellarmine.html). second, the de fide dogma of the visibility and permanence of the church and of her petrine office, formulated in pastor aeternus chapter 2 (ds 3056-3058), mt 28:20, and pius xii, mystici corporis christi (1943, aas 35, 199-248). third, that according to catholic doctrine a pope in formal heresy is not impossible; otherwise bellarmine’s whole discussion would be without object. from the first and third propositions it seems to follow that a non-universally recognized vacancy of the see would be possible, which would violate the second proposition, for a hidden sedevacantist state with all practical consequences, from invalid cardinal appointments to the potential rupture of apostolic succession, would no longer allow the church to remain visibly in being. my solution draws on the old theological principle ecclesia supplet , in german “kirchliche suppletion der jurisdiktion,” the church’s supplying of jurisdiction. if an orthodox or schismatic priest who formally stands outside the visible unity of the church can validly and licitly administer sacraments to catholics in danger of death, as canon 844 §2 cic/1983 expressly recognizes and as was already recognized in the theological manuals before the code (cf. suarez, de censuris disp. xv; cajetan, commentaria in summam theologiae iii, q. 64, a. 9; prummer, manuale theologiae moralis iii, n. 285), then this does not rest on a jurisdictional power still remaining in him himself, but on a supplementation by the church herself ad necessitatem . bellarmine’s statement that in the heretic there remains no spiritual power over those who remain in the church (cited in de rom. pont. ii, 30) refers to the heretic’s own jurisdiction, which he can no longer hold of himself, not to the possibility that the church supplements his acts for the preservation of the higher good. otherwise even the supply to the orthodox priest would be excluded, which is obviously not ecclesial practice. the deeper principle is a combination of three elements. first, salus animarum suprema lex (can. 1752 cic/1983), the salvation of souls as the supreme law to which the positive canonical order is subordinated. second, that the petrine office is instituted propter homines , that is, that its purpose lies in the salvation of the faithful and not in the disposal of the officeholder; from this ordering to an end it follows, according to suarez, that the church can by her own power supply what is necessary to attain this end ( de censuris disp. xv). third, the bonum commune ecclesiae , which in an unprecedented ecclesial crisis requires the continued existence of visible structures. if the church can fulfill her dogmatically guaranteed visible permanence only by supplying to a materially designated but, because of formal heresy, personally office-incapable pope the jurisdictional acts necessary for continuity, then this supply is not an arbitrary expansion of ecclesia supplet , but required by the basic principle itself. this supply is narrowly limited. it does not supplement the whole magisterium with all its implications, but only those acts necessary for preserving visible continuity, namely cardinal appointments for the continuity of papal election, the ratification of valid episcopal consecrations, and valid liturgical promulgations. what is not supplied is teaching authority for heretical statements, because these contradict the purpose for whose sake the supply takes place at all. true statements of such an acting pope are to be accepted, but not by reason of his office, which he no longer holds of himself, but by reason of truth itself. the narrowly defined infallibility from pastor aeternus chapter 4 (ds 3074) remains untouched, moreover, because it follows from the infallibility of the church and from the position as head, which is preserved through supply quoad effectum ; a pope who errs only materially or is formally heretical will empirically avoid ex cathedra acts anyway, because their formal requirements - universal binding force and definitive character - collide with his inner disposition. the supply ends as soon as the state of emergency is ended. this occurs when the church formally establishes the heretic as such and thus the visibility no longer has to be preserved through his person. this is not conciliarism, because a council does not set itself above a pope, but declaratively establishes that the man in question is ex hypothesi not pope. from this moment bellarmine’s thesis ipso facto applies without a safety mechanism; the church no longer supplies, because she can now fulfill her duty to visible continuity through a regular election. it is important for me to stress that this construction does not have to be invoked for the present situation of the fsspx. the position i defended above holds the post-conciliar popes to be material, not formal, errants, in analogy to maximus’s defense of honorius. thus bellarmine’s condition is not triggered in the first place, and no supply is needed. the solution sketched here is intended only as a hypothetical reserve argument in case someone did not want to apply the material/formal distinction to these popes; it shows that even then sedevacantism does not necessarily follow. it is also my own thesis, which in this form does not belong to the standard repertoire of traditional theology, but remains structurally related to the cassiciacum tradition and reconstructible from classical principles ( salus animarum , propter homines , bonum commune ecclesiae ).

providence.de: vorsehung und freier wille der widerspruch gottes allwissenheit verlangt, dass notwendigerweise fur jede aussage x, wenn x wahr ist, gott x weiss. also: \[ \forall x: \box (x \rightarrow w(g,x)) \] 1 freier wille verlangt, dass fur jede freie willensentscheidung y, es moglich gewesen ware, sich nicht fur y zu entscheiden. also: \[ \forall y: (y \in fw) \rightarrow \diamond \neg y \] 2 diese bedingung ist notwendig aber nicht ausreichend um eine entscheidung als freie willensentscheidung zu charakterisieren. ein programmierbarer roboter mit eine if else statement, welches abhangig ist vom zufalligen zerfall eines radioaktiven partikels, erfullt die obige bedingung, konstituiert allerdings noch immer keine freie willensentscheidung. eine zusatzliche notwendige bedingung ist, dass die person die die entscheidung trifft, die determinierende ursache der entscheidung ist. also: \[ \forall y: (y \in fw) \rightarrow \exists z: y \iff u(z,y) \] 3 um nicht sagen zu mussen, dass der radioaktive partikel eine freie willensentscheidung getroffen hat mussen wir noch hinzufugen, dass z der start der kausalen kette der willensentscheidung sein muss, bzw. zumindest keine determinierende ursache, in der kausalen kette vor z stehen darf. (in diesem fall ware es eine determinierende ursache mit probabilistischem effekt). nun zeigt sich hier langsam der wiederspruch zur allwissenheit gottes, wenn gott richtigerweise in aristotelischer/thomistischer tradition als absolut simpel verstanden wird. der thomistische gott hat keine (passive) potenz, also kann auch sein wissen nur aktiv sein. 4 eine gute analogie ist sich vorzustellen, dass man ohne einen ball zu beobachten, genau seine position kennen wurde, wenn man nur die umwelteinflusse und physikalischen gesetze perfekt kennen wurde, und selbst den ball werfen wurde. die position durch beobachtung zu kennen ware passives wissen, dadurch sich selbst, seinen akt der werfens perfekt zu kennen, sowie perfektes wissen uber die welt zu haben und dadurch die position des balls zu kennen ware aktives wissen. nun muss gott allerdings um freie willensentscheidungen zu kennen auch deren ursache sein und um sie notwendiger weise zu kennen, ihre determinierende ursache sein. somit waren die bedingungen, dass y eine freie willensentscheidung ist zwar immer noch gegeben, aber es ware gottes freier wille der die entscheidung trifft. dies wurde bedeuten, dass auch gott moralisch verantwortlich ist und gott konnte niemanden gerechterweise in die holle schicken. einer von vielen widerspruchen zur biblischen und katholischen lehre den wir vermeiden mussen. um das dilemma noch expliziter zu formulieren: was ist der truth-maker 5 von y? ist der mensch der truth-maker, dann hat gott kein perfektes wissen, ist gott der truth-maker, ist der mensch nicht frei, ist es eine kombination aus beiden bleibt dass dilemma, da bei unterschiedlichen entscheidungen eine die andere “stechen muss”. molinismus der molinismus versucht das problem uber “middle knowledge” zu losen: gott weiss wie jeder mensch in jeder situation reagieren wurde, da er die tatsachlichen umstande kennt weiss er also auch wie der mensch in der echten welt handelt bzw. welche entscheidung er trifft. allein die moglichkeit von middle knowledge scheint der ersten voraussetzung fur freien willen zu widersprechen. sie schein vorauszusetzen, dass in jeder moglichen welt notwendigerweise y oder nicht y. um er anders zu formulieren, was ist der truth-maker der propositionen in der menge von gottes middle knowledge? wir landen wieder beim selben dilemma, bei dem hier der freie wille des menschen der allwissenheit gottes geopfert wird. position von banez dieser position kann ich nicht viel aufmerksamkeit schenken. einfach zu sagen, dass gott per physical premotions die determinierende ursachen eine entscheidung sein kann ohne, dass sie dadurch weniger freie willensentscheidung des menschen ist, macht es nicht weniger zu einem offensichtlichen oxymoron. open theism die losung heisst open theism. gott ist wie ein programmierer eines videospiels, in dem der spieler selbst entscheidungen treffen kann. er kennt den kompletten quellcode, er weiss wann der spieler welche entscheidungen treffen kann und wie die welt in jedem fall aussieht. er kann auch vorplanen, wie er einschreiten wird abhangig von den entscheidungen des spielers. er kennt alle moglichen aste des entscheidungsbaumes. um ein bisschen von der analogie wegzukommen und konkret von gott zu sprechen: gott hat drei arten von wissen: notwendiges internes wissen, echtes internes wissen und externes wissen. notwendiges internes wissen umfasst notwendige wahrheiten, wie tautologien, mathematische wahrheiten, wissen uber seine notwendige natur und auch (aus dem letzten punkt folgend) wissen uber aller moglichen welten. (da er sich perfekt kennt weiss er alle mogliche arten, in der seine schopfung ihn reflektieren konnte). echtes internes wissen weiss gott, da er in seinem absolut simplen wesen gleich mit seinem schopfungsakt ist, einer freien willensentscheidung. er weiss alle physikalisch notwendigen wahrheiten, die zusammensetzung des universums im moment der schopfung und alle seine direkten eingriffe in die welt unter den entsprechenden umstanden. freie willensentscheidungen fallen unter externes wissen. externes wissen alle wahren aussagen die nicht internes wissen gottes sind, sind sein externes wissen. sie beschreiben, die relation der geschaffenen welt zu gott. wenn x wahr ist und nicht internes wissen gottes ist konnen wir sagen, dass gott x weiss, insofern er die (erste und) erhaltende ursache des truth-makers von x ist und abhangig von x agieren kann. unabhangig von seiner haltung zu open theism muss der thomist glauben, dass zumindest ein teil von gottes wissen externes wissen ist. ich werde spater ein paar argumente gegen eternalism geben. ist presentism oder die growing block theory of time wahr, dann hat die gegenwart eine objektive qualitat. somit haben auch fakten objektive wahrheitswerte, die abhangig von der gegenwart sind. “olaf scholz ist bundeskanzler der bundesrepublik deutschland” ist somit eine aussagen mit einem objektiven wahrheitswert, der sich mit der zeit andert. qua objektive wahrheit muss gott ihn kennen, aber qua sich zeitlich andernd kann er nicht intern zu gott sein. also ist etabliert, dass der thomist dazu verpflichtet ist, dass zumindest diese art von aussagen unter gottes externes wissen fallen. open theism verlangt lediglich, dass freie willensentscheidungen (und teilweise ihre konsequenzen) auch in diese gruppe fallen. einwand 1: externes wissen ist nicht wirklich wissen der einwand ware hier, dass es inkorrekt ware zu sagen, dass gott x tatsachlich weiss nur, weil er 1. erste und erhaltende ursache von x ist 2. abhangig von x agieren kann. dieser einwand ist nicht wirklich falsch, wir sagen nicht, dass tatsachlich so etwas wie wissen in gott ist. aber wir sagen auch nicht, dass so etwas wie starke in gott ist. als thomisten ist gott einfach sein akt der existenz und beinhaltet keine differenzierbaren attribute. zu sagen, dass gott etwas weiss ist, wird fur den thomisten immer anders sein, als das ein geschopf etwas weiss. der hier behandelte einwand (der meiner meinung nach offensichtlichste und starkste) entsteht auf dem fehler unsere art des wissens zu univocal auf gott zu ubertragen und nicht analog . 6 moglicherweise befriedigt diese definition von externem wissen sogar die vom heiligen thomas uber gottes wissen von zukunftigen kontingenten dingen. 7 unsere definition befriedigt zumindest in einer gewissen lesart vom heiligen thomas die bedingungen, dass gott future contingents sowohl in ihren ursachen (insoweit er ihre erste ursache ist) als auch in ihrer existenz (insoweit er erhaltende ursache ist und ihre essenz eine teilweise reflektion seiner eigenen essenz ist) selbst kennt. einwand 2: prophetie es scheint als konnte gott basierend auf seinem externen wissen nicht prophezeien. das stimmt, gott weiss die propositionen in der menge seines externen wissens nicht auf die art, als das er sie alle zu einem vorherigen zeitpunkt offenbaren konnte ohne zu lugen. gott hat allerdings viele moglichkeiten (analog eines videospiel-programmierers) den lauf der dinge zu lenken. er kann die wahlmoglichkeiten einschranken, zwischen denen der freie mensch entscheiden kann, er kann auf gewisse arten (die sie ja in ihrem buch beschreiben) auf den freien willen einwirken, und er kann den freien willen auch uberschreiben (in welchem fall der mensch nicht mehr moralisch verantwortlich ist). so kann gott den lauf der welt auf gewisse fixe events lenken, die er dann schon zuvor offenbaren kann. auch wenn man keine open theist ist, muss man glauben, dass gottes prophetie beschrankt ist. unter molinismus ist es moglich, dass z nur x entscheidet, wenn x ihm nicht zuvor offenbart wird. also kann gott z nicht x offenbaren. als anhanger von banez scheint man zumindest von unendlichkeits-bernadette-paradoxa eingeschrankt zu sein. 8 meine art des open theism kombiniert mit meiner bevorzugten zeit theorie durfte diese paradoxa umgehen. biblische unterstutzung fur open theism das open theism meiner meinung nach die einzige theorie ist, die einen allwissenden absolut simplen gott und einen tatsachlich freien menschen philosophisch konsistent unter einen hut bringen kann war schon genug um mich von der theorie zu uberzeugen. allerdings glaube ich auch, dass prima facia open theism die naturliche biblische theorie von gottes vorsehung ist. die bibel ist voll von beispielen, wo gott menschen testet bzw. auf die probe stellt. nur unter open theism sind dies tatsachlich tests. unter molinismus weiss gott eh schon wie jede person in jeder situation reagiert, und unter der position von banez ist es gar nicht der mensch der letztendlich die entscheidung trifft. naturlich lasst sich auch unter diesen positionen ein zweck fur diese tests finden, dies ist dann allerdings nicht die naturliche prima facia lesung des biblischen tests. ich halte dies tatsachlich fur ein ausserst starkes argument fur open theism, dessen kraft leider dadurch untergraben wird, wie kurz dieser absatz ist. abschliessende gedanken ich hatte leider immer noch keine zeit ihr buch zu lesen, herr pater deneke. von dem was ich allerdings gelesen habe war ich sehr sehr positiv uberrascht. ich habe das gefuhl, dass sie einer der wenigen philosophen sind, der diesem thema intellektuell ehrlich begegnet. sie scheinen die theorie tatsachlich selbst durchzudenken und versuchen nicht nur irgendwie die theorie ihres lieblingsphilosophen zwanghaft zu verteidigen (wie ed feser es manchmal zu tun scheint). auch, dass sie kein problem damit haben (im richtigen verstandnis) zuzulassen, dass gott sich einschranken kann fand ich sehr positiv. ich wurde vermuten, dass meine theorie das auch verlangt. um meine denkweise besser zu verstehen lohnt es sich dual agency: a thomistic account of providence and human freedom von rob koons 9 zu lesen. ich stimme praktisch allem zu bis seite 13 (und den gegenargumenten gegen seine eigene position, die er auf seite 14 prasentiert), speziell auch in seiner kritik des molinismus. auch stimme ich seinem lob von van invagens kritik an kompatibalismus zu. koons theorie verliert mich, da er offensichtlich keinen 1. moglichen, 2. plausiblen, 3. und gemeinsamen truth-maker von (2) und (3) identifizieren kann. und somit schon gar nicht einen, der plausibler weise nicht den freien willen des menschen einschrankt. ich werde nun noch zeigen, wie ich zwei theologische grundsatze versuche in meiner theorie zu erklaren. abschliessend werde ich noch ganz kurz meine argumente zu zeit theorien prasentieren. verrat von judas wie konnte jesus beim letzten abendmahl den verrat von judas voraussehen? ich glaube, dass judas mit vielen sundigen entscheidungen zuvor seine seele so verdunkelt hat und seinen freien willen damit so eingeschrankt hat, dass er in der entsprechenden situation nicht mehr anders konnte als gott zu verraten. jesus wusste es im voraus, da judas’ freier wille so eingeschrankt war und judas ist dennoch verantwortlich, da er seinen freien willen selbst durch vorausgegangene entscheidungen so eingeschrankt hat. sunde ist eben wie sucht, mit der man durch freie willensentscheidungen in eine negativ spirale gelangt, in der man seinen freien willen immer mehr einschrankt. sundenfreiheit mariens es scheint als hatte gott zum zeitpunkt der verkundigung gewusst, dass maria frei von sunde bleiben wird. wie kann maria dafur ruhmenswert (also verantwortlich) sein und gott es dennoch zuvor wissen? hier konnte man argumentieren, dass meine theorie zusammenbricht, allerdings glaube ich nicht, dass die anderen theorien einen erklarenden vorteil haben. ich vermute, dass gott marias seele vor ihrer zeugung geschaffen hat und den engeln gleich vor eine entscheidung gestellt hat ihm zu folgen. durch ihr “ja” hat er sie bei ihrer zeugung und spater bei allen entscheidungen vor der sunde bewahrt. so wusste er von ihrer sundenlosigkeit und sie bleibt durch ihr “ja” vor ihrer zeugung dennoch ruhmenswert. mir ist bewusst dass dies sehr unorthodox (im umgangssprachlichen sinne nicht im sinne von heterodox) erscheint. allerdings hat diese theorie mir geholfen maria mehr zu lieben da wir so im aller wahrsten sinne wirklich ihren verdienst an der inkarnation begreifen konnen. unter anderen theorien scheint sie nicht wirklich ruhmenswert wenn sie sagt “mir geschehe nach deinem worte”. daruber lohnt es sich im gebet zu reflektieren. zeit theorien durch die natur von akt und potenz ist presentism auch nach meinung von ed feser die naturliche position des thomisten. 10 eternalism scheint zu fatalism zu fuhren, wie aristoteles in seinem argument mit der seeschlacht ausfuhrt. 11 unter presentism kann diese aussage keinen wahrheitswert haben, da sie in keiner korrespondenz zu etwas tatsachlich existentem stehen kann, da die zukunft reine potenz ist. so wird fatalism umgangen. gleichzeitig verlieren unter diesem argument aber vergangene fakten ihren wahrheitswert. die growing block theory of time hingegen bewahrt unter der korrespondenz theorie der wahrheit den wahrheitswert von vergangenen fakten ohne sich zu wahrheitswerten fur future contingents zu verpflichten. w(g,x) bedeutet hier gott w eiss x ↩︎ fw ist die menge der freien willensentscheidungen ↩︎ u(z,y) bedeutet hier z ist die determinierende u rsache von y ↩︎ siehe auch providence.en: providence and free will the contradiction divine omniscience requires that, necessarily, for every proposition \(x\) , if \(x\) is true, god knows \(x\) : \[ \forall x: \box (x \rightarrow k(g,x)) \] 1 free will requires that, for every free decision \(y\) , it would have been possible not to choose \(y\) : \[ \forall y: (y \in fw) \rightarrow \diamond \neg y \] 2 this condition is necessary but not sufficient to characterize an act as free. a programmable robot with an if–else statement that depends on the random decay of a radioactive particle satisfies the condition above, but it still does not make a free decision. a further necessary condition is that the person making the decision is its determining cause: \[ \forall y: (y \in fw) \rightarrow \exists z: y \iff c(z,y) \] 3 to avoid saying that the radioactive particle has made a free decision, we must add that \(z\) begins the relevant causal chain, or at least that no determining cause precedes \(z\) within that chain. otherwise there would merely be a determining cause with a probabilistic effect. the tension with divine omniscience emerges once god is understood, correctly in the aristotelian-thomistic tradition, as absolutely simple. the thomistic god has no passive potency, so his knowledge can only be active. 4 imagine knowing the exact position of a ball without observing it because you threw it yourself and know both the environmental influences and the physical laws perfectly. knowing its position by observation would be passive knowledge. knowing it through perfect knowledge of yourself, of your act of throwing, and of the world would be active knowledge. yet if god is to know free decisions in this way, he must be their cause; and if he knows them necessarily, he appears to be their determining cause. the formal conditions above might still call \(y\) a free decision, but it would be god’s will, not the creature’s, making the decision. god would then be morally responsible and could not justly condemn anyone. that is one of several conflicts with biblical and catholic teaching that we must avoid. the dilemma can be stated more explicitly: what is the truth-maker of \(y\) ? 5 if the human being is the truth-maker, god seems to lack perfect knowledge. if god is the truth-maker, the human being is not free. if both are involved, the dilemma remains, because in divergent decisions one determining contribution must ultimately prevail over the other. molinism molinism attempts to solve the problem through middle knowledge : god knows how every person would respond in every possible situation. since he knows the actual circumstances, he therefore knows how that person acts in the actual world. the very possibility of middle knowledge seems to conflict with the first condition of free will. it appears to presuppose that in every possible world either \(y\) or \(\neg y\) is necessary. put differently: what makes the counterfactual propositions contained in god’s middle knowledge true? we arrive at the same dilemma, with human freedom sacrificed to divine omniscience. banez’s position i cannot give this view much attention here. merely asserting that god can, by means of physical premotions , be the determining cause of a decision without thereby making it any less the person’s free decision does not make the apparent oxymoron disappear. open theism the proposed solution is open theism. god is analogous to the programmer of a game in which the player can make genuine decisions. the programmer knows the whole source code, every point at which the player can choose, and what the world will look like after each choice. he can plan how to intervene in response to the player’s decisions. he knows every possible branch of the decision tree. leaving the analogy and speaking directly about god, we can distinguish three kinds of divine knowledge: necessary internal knowledge, actual internal knowledge, and external knowledge. necessary internal knowledge encompasses necessary truths: tautologies, mathematical truths, knowledge of god’s necessary nature, and—following from the latter—knowledge of every possible world. since god perfectly knows himself, he knows every possible way in which creation could reflect him. god has actual internal knowledge because, in his absolutely simple being, he is identical with his act of creation, which is a free act. he knows every physically necessary truth, the constitution of the universe at the moment of creation, and all of his own direct interventions under the relevant conditions. free decisions belong to external knowledge. external knowledge every true proposition that is not part of god’s internal knowledge belongs to his external knowledge. such propositions describe the relation of the created world to god. if \(x\) is true but not internal to god, we may say that god knows \(x\) insofar as he is the first and sustaining cause of the truth-maker of \(x\) , and can act in dependence on \(x\) . whatever one thinks of open theism, a thomist must hold that at least some divine knowledge is external in this sense. i give several arguments against eternalism below. if presentism or the growing-block theory of time is true, the present has an objective status. facts then have objective truth-values that depend on the present. “olaf scholz is chancellor of the federal republic of germany,” for example, is a proposition whose objective truth-value changes with time. insofar as it is objectively true, god must know it; insofar as it changes over time, it cannot be internal to god. the thomist is therefore committed to placing at least this kind of proposition within god’s external knowledge. open theism asks only that free decisions—and sometimes their consequences—belong to this class as well. objection 1: external knowledge is not really knowledge the objection is that it would be incorrect to say god actually knows \(x\) merely because he: is the first and sustaining cause of \(x\) ; and can act in dependence on \(x\) . this objection is not simply mistaken. we are not saying that there is literally some distinct thing called knowledge in god—but neither do we say that there is a distinct thing called strength in him. for the thomist, god is his act of existence and contains no differentiable attributes. to say that god knows something will always differ from saying that a creature knows something. the objection—probably the most obvious and forceful one—arises from applying our mode of knowledge to god univocally rather than analogically . 6 this definition of external knowledge may even satisfy st. thomas’s account of divine knowledge of future contingents. 7 on at least one reading of thomas, our definition preserves his conditions: god knows future contingents both in their causes, insofar as he is their first cause, and in their existence, insofar as he is their sustaining cause and their essences partially reflect his own. objection 2: prophecy it seems that god could not prophesy on the basis of external knowledge. in one respect that is correct: god does not know all propositions in the set of his external knowledge in a way that permits him to reveal every one of them at an earlier moment without falsehood. yet, like the programmer in the analogy, god has many ways of directing events. he can restrict the alternatives among which a free person chooses; he can influence the will in various ways; and he can override it, in which case the person is no longer morally responsible. god can therefore guide history toward certain fixed events and reveal them in advance. even those who reject open theism must admit limits of this kind. under molinism it may be true that \(z\) chooses \(x\) only if \(x\) is not revealed to \(z\) beforehand; god then cannot reveal \(x\) to \(z\) . a follower of banez appears at least to face infinity-bernadette paradoxes . 8 my form of open theism, combined with my preferred theory of time, should avoid these paradoxes. biblical support for open theism the philosophical claim that open theism is the only theory capable of consistently combining an omniscient, absolutely simple god with genuinely free human beings was already sufficient to persuade me. yet i also think open theism is, prima facie , the natural biblical account of providence. scripture is full of episodes in which god tests human beings. only under open theism are these tests in the most straightforward sense genuine tests. under molinism, god already knows exactly how each person would respond in every circumstance; under banez’s position, the human being is not ultimately the one determining the decision. other purposes can of course be assigned to biblical tests within those systems, but such explanations are not their natural prima facie reading. i regard this as an exceptionally strong argument for open theism, even if the brevity of this paragraph understates its force. concluding thoughts father deneke, i unfortunately have still not had time to read your book in full. what i have read, however, surprised me very positively. you appear to be one of the few philosophers who approaches this subject with genuine intellectual honesty: you seem to think the theory through for yourself rather than forcing a defense of a favored philosopher’s system—as ed feser sometimes seems to do. i was also encouraged that you allow, properly understood, that god can limit himself. i suspect my theory requires this as well. to understand my approach better, it is worth reading rob koons’s “dual agency: a thomistic account of providence and human freedom.” 9 i agree with nearly everything through page 13, especially koons’s criticism of molinism, and with the objections he raises against his own position on page 14. i also agree with his praise for van inwagen’s critique of compatibilism. koons’s theory loses me because it does not identify a truth-maker that is simultaneously: possible; plausible; and common to propositions (2) and (3). it therefore certainly does not identify one that plausibly preserves human freedom. i will now show how i attempt to explain two basic theological doctrines within my account, and conclude with a brief presentation of my arguments concerning theories of time. the betrayal of judas how could jesus foresee judas’s betrayal at the last supper? i believe that, through many prior sinful decisions, judas had so darkened his soul and narrowed his own freedom that, in the decisive situation, he could no longer do otherwise than betray god. jesus knew the betrayal in advance because judas’s freedom had become so restricted; judas nevertheless remained responsible because he had brought about that restriction through his own earlier decisions. sin resembles addiction: by a sequence of free choices, one enters a downward spiral in which one progressively constrains one’s freedom. mary’s sinlessness it appears that at the annunciation god knew mary would remain free from sin. how can mary deserve praise—and thus be responsible—if god knew this beforehand? one might argue that my theory fails here, but i do not think the competing theories possess an explanatory advantage. i suspect that god created mary’s soul before her conception and, as with the angels, placed before her a choice to follow him. through her “yes,” he preserved her from sin at her conception and in every later decision. god therefore knew her sinlessness, while she remained praiseworthy because of her pre-conception “yes.” i am aware that this sounds highly unorthodox—in the colloquial sense, not necessarily in the sense of heterodox. yet the theory has helped me love mary more, because it lets us understand her contribution to the incarnation as merit in the fullest possible sense. under other theories she can seem less genuinely praiseworthy when she says, “let it be done to me according to your word.” this is worth reflecting upon in prayer. theories of time given the nature of act and potency, presentism is, in ed feser’s view as well, the natural thomistic position. 10 eternalism appears to lead to fatalism, as aristotle suggests in his sea-battle argument. 11 under presentism, a proposition about a future contingent event cannot yet have a truth-value, because it cannot correspond to anything actually existent: the future is pure potency. fatalism is thereby avoided. on the same reasoning, however, past facts lose their truth-values as well. the growing-block theory of time preserves, within a correspondence theory of truth, the truth of past facts without committing us to present truth-values for future contingents. here, \(k(g,x)\) means that god k nows \(x\) . ↩︎ \(fw\) is the set of free acts of will. ↩︎ here, \(c(z,y)\) means that \(z\) is the determining c ause of \(y\) . ↩︎ see summa theologiae i, q. 14, a. 8 . ↩︎ i do not mean to commit myself here to a comprehensive theory of truth-makers; i use the term in the basic sense supplied by a correspondence theory of truth. ↩︎ see summa theologiae i, q. 13, a. 5 . ↩︎ see summa theologiae i, q. 14, a. 13 . ↩︎ see schmid 2023 in mind , doi:10.1093/mind/fzad065 ; this claim requires further study. ↩︎ doi:10.5840/pc20024241; a free copy
